page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance equipped with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. Built on a KVM hypervisor with dedicated CPU allocation, the server exposes 12 physical cores and 24 vCPUs with two threads per core. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory is provisioned at 48.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration includes 8 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. It contains no bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, relying entirely on remote block storage resources.

Performance profiles reflect strong multi-threaded execution balanced by lower single-threaded efficiency. Benchmarks register average multi-core capabilities, including a PassMark CPU score of 21,643.62 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 8,967.0. Memory bandwidth tests yield uncached read speeds of 108.94 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 47.99 GB/sec. Specialized workloads demonstrate 20.09 million Redis SET operations per second and static web serving throughput of 15.86 GB/sec. Single-core performance falls into lower performance bands, recorded at 1,313.3 in stress-ng single-core tests and 22.86 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression.

Hardware instruction extensions include AVX, AVX-512 (f and vnni), AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. The strict 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation maximizes core density while minimizing idle RAM capacity cost overheads. The instance presents a clear tradeoff between single-thread responsiveness and parallel compute output. The server profile is optimized for multi-threaded web application backends, software compilation, CI/CD pipelines, batch processing, and medium-scale database operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor featuring 12 physical cores and 24 vCPUs. It provides 48.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and relies entirely on network storage as no local disks or GPUs are included. Benchmarks demonstrate average multi-core performance across Geekbench and PassMark alongside a Redis SET throughput of 20.09 million operations per second, though single-core execution shows weaker efficiency in stress-ng and compression tests. Supported by hardware instruction sets including AVX-512 VNNI and AES, this instance offers high core density for parallel compute tasks without unused RAM overhead. It is well suited for multi-threaded application servers, CI/CD build environments, batch processing, and medium-scale database workloads.
